grades.quote: |63|RPLV|RW|Restricted Privilege LeVel enable (RPLV) of the page table. When RPLV=0, the page table entry can be accessed by any program whose privilege level is not lower than PLV; when RPLV=1, the page table entry can only be accessed by programs whose privilege level is equal to PLV.|
grades.reason: The LA64 TLBELO0/TLBELO1 table (the one with PALEN and bit 63) defines RPLV. RPLV=0 lets any program access the entry if its privilege level is not lower than PLV. RPLV=1 lets only programs whose privilege level equals PLV access it. This directly answers how RPLV changes the check.

grades.reason: The LA64 TLBRELO0/TLBRELO1 table gives the same RPLV semantics. RPLV=0 means access by privilege level not lower than PLV, and RPLV=1 means access only at a privilege level equal to PLV. The register is the refill-context copy of the TLB entry low bits, but the passage still answers the question.
